title: The conditional
description: Ask politely, give advice, make wishes and imagine with “would”.
rule: Form the conditional with the future stem plus the imparfait endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je parlerais, nous finirions, ils prendraient. Verbs with an irregular future stem keep it: je serais, j’aurais, j’irais, je ferais, je pourrais, je voudrais, je devrais, je saurais, je viendrais, il faudrait. Use it to ask or offer politely (je voudrais un café, pourriez-vous m’aider ?), to give advice with devoir (tu devrais dormir), to express a wish (j’aimerais voyager), and for something imagined or only possible (à ta place, je partirais). Do not confuse the conditional with the future and the imparfait: je parlerais means I would speak, je parlerai means I will speak, and je parlais means I was speaking or used to speak. Only the conditional has both the r of the future stem and an imparfait ending.
example: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît. · Tu devrais dormir un peu. · À ta place, je partirais.
aside: Je parlerai and je parlerais often sound the same, so the spelling has to show the meaning: will or would.

alternatives.message: Parlerai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Take the future stem and add the je ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: The conditional is the future stem plus the imparfait endings.
exercises.explanation: Parler- + -ais gives je parlerais.

alternatives.message: Finirons is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.
Finissions is the imparfait. The conditional keeps the future stem finir-.

exercises.hint: Start from the future stem and add the nous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Check that you have both the r of the future stem and the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Finir- + -ions gives nous finirions.

exercises.hint: Prendre loses its final e in the future stem. Then add the ils ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem prendr- with the imparfait ending for ils.
exercises.explanation: Prendr- + -aient gives ils prendraient.

exercises.source: Avec une voiture, vous ____ (voyager) plus souvent.
exercises.hint: Future stem plus the vous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: The vous ending of the conditional is -iez, after the future stem.
exercises.explanation: Voyager- + -iez gives vous voyageriez.

exercises.source: Elles ____ bien un peu de thé.
exercises.hint: Check the stem of prendre and the ending for elles.
exercises.feedback: The conditional is prendr- plus the imparfait ending for elles.
exercises.explanation: Elles prendraient: stem prendr-, ending -aient.

exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: The ending does not match tu.
exercises.explanation: With tu, the conditional ends in -ais: tu marcherais.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the conditional.
exercises.source: We would gladly live in the countryside.
answers: Nous habiterions volontiers à la campagne.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of habiter. The conditional keeps the r of the future stem.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the imparfait, not the conditional.
exercises.explanation: Habiter- + -ions gives nous habiterions. Habitions is the imparfait.

alternatives.message: Serai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Être uses the same irregular stem as in the future.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of être with the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Ser- + -ais gives je serais.

exercises.hint: Faire uses the same irregular stem as in the future.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of faire with the vous ending -iez.
exercises.explanation: Fer- + -iez gives vous feriez.

exercises.hint: Venir uses the same irregular stem as in the future.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of venir with the imparfait ending for elle.
exercises.explanation: Viendr- + -ait gives elle viendrait.

exercises.hint: Il faut has an irregular future stem. Keep it and add the il ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of falloir with -ait.
exercises.explanation: Faudr- + -ait gives il faudrait.

exercises.source: À ta place, j’____ chez le médecin.
exercises.hint: À ta place describes something imagined. Aller has an irregular future stem.
exercises.feedback: Use the conditional, built on the irregular stem of aller.
exercises.explanation: Imagined situations take the conditional: ir- + -ais gives j’irais.

exercises.source: Avec plus d’argent, nous averions une grande maison.
answers: Avec plus d’argent, nous aurions une grande maison.
exercises.hint: Avoir has an irregular stem in the future and the conditional.
exercises.feedback: The stem of avoir is wrong.
exercises.explanation: The conditional of avoir uses the stem aur-: nous aurions.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. It refers to a situation, not to a particular thing.
exercises.hint: Use être in the conditional with ce.
exercises.feedback: Être has an irregular stem in the conditional.
exercises.explanation: Ser- + -ait gives ce serait.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the conditional.
exercises.hint: Pouvoir has an irregular future stem with a double r.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of pouvoir with the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Pourr- + -ait gives elle pourrait.

exercises.source: Bonjour, je ____ un café, s’il vous plaît.
exercises.hint: A polite request uses the conditional. Check the ending for je.
exercises.feedback: Look for the conditional of vouloir with the je ending.
exercises.explanation: Je voudrais is the conditional of vouloir, the polite way to ask. Voudrai is the future.

exercises.instruction: Make the request more polite: put the verb in the conditional and keep the inversion.
exercises.hint: Pouvoir has an irregular stem in the conditional.
exercises.feedback: Change pouvez into the conditional vous form.
exercises.explanation: Pourr- + -iez gives pourriez-vous, a more polite request.

exercises.instruction: Make it polite: put the verb in the conditional.
exercises.source: Je veux une chambre pour deux nuits.
answers: Je voudrais une chambre pour deux nuits.
exercises.hint: Vouloir has an irregular stem with a d.
exercises.feedback: Change veux into the conditional je form.
exercises.explanation: Je veux sounds blunt; je voudrais is the polite conditional.

answers: Est-ce que vous pourriez fermer la porte ?

alternatives.message: That is correct but less polite. Could is the conditional: pourriez-vous.

exercises.hint: Could here is the conditional of pouvoir.
exercises.feedback: Use the vous form of pouvoir in the conditional.
exercises.explanation: Pourriez-vous is the polite conditional of pouvoir.

exercises.instruction: Write pouvoir in the conditional (vous form).
exercises.source: ____-vous me dire l’heure, s’il vous plaît ?

alternatives.message: Right form, but -vous is already in the sentence. Write only the missing word.

exercises.hint: Future stem of pouvoir plus the vous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Pouvoir has an irregular stem with a double r.
exercises.explanation: Pourr- + -iez gives pourriez-vous.

exercises.source: I would like to speak to the manager.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of vouloir. Only one means would like.
exercises.feedback: The polite form is the conditional, ending in -ais.
exercises.explanation: Je voudrais is the conditional; je voudrai is the future.

exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: The ending does not match vous.
exercises.explanation: With vous, the conditional ends in -iez: pourriez-vous.

alternatives.message: Devras is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Devoir has an irregular future stem. Add the tu ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem devr- with the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Devr- + -ais gives tu devrais.

exercises.hint: Advice uses devoir in the conditional. Check the stem and the ending for tu.
exercises.feedback: Look for the irregular stem of devoir and the tu ending.
exercises.explanation: Tu devrais (you should) is devr- + -ais.

exercises.source: Vous toussez beaucoup. Vous ____ (devoir) arrêter de fumer.
exercises.hint: This is advice. Use the irregular stem and the vous ending.
exercises.feedback: Advice uses the conditional of devoir.
exercises.explanation: Devr- + -iez gives vous devriez, you should.

exercises.source: You (to a friend) should call your mother.
answers: Tu devrais téléphoner à ta mère.

alternatives.message: Dois means must. Should is the conditional of devoir: tu devrais.

alternatives.answer: Tu dois téléphoner à ta mère.
alternatives.message: Dois means must. Should is the conditional of devoir: tu devrais.

exercises.hint: Should is devoir in the conditional, followed by an infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Use the conditional of devoir, not the present.
exercises.explanation: Tu devrais + infinitive gives advice: tu devrais appeler ta mère.

exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: The ending does not match il.
exercises.explanation: With il, the conditional ends in -ait: il devrait.

exercises.instruction: Turn this order into advice: start with Tu and use devoir in the conditional.
exercises.hint: The command becomes an infinitive after the conditional of devoir.
exercises.feedback: Use tu + devoir in the conditional + infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Mange ! becomes the softer advice tu devrais manger.

exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of devoir. Only one means should.
exercises.feedback: Advice uses the conditional, not the future.
exercises.explanation: Vous devriez is the conditional (should); vous devrez is the future (will have to).

alternatives.message: Aimerons is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Future stem of aimer plus the nous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Check that you have both the r of the stem and the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Aimer- + -ions gives nous aimerions.

exercises.source: J’____ bien visiter le Japon un jour.
exercises.hint: This is a wish, and the subject is je.
exercises.feedback: A wish uses the conditional of aimer with the je ending.
exercises.explanation: J’aimerais (I would like) is aimer- + -ais.

exercises.source: Mes parents ____ (aimer) vivre au bord de la mer.
exercises.hint: Mes parents is ils. Future stem plus the imparfait ending.
exercises.feedback: The ils ending of the conditional is -aient.
exercises.explanation: Aimer- + -aient gives ils aimeraient.

alternatives.message: J’aimerai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.
Je voudrai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Would like is aimer or vouloir in the conditional.
exercises.feedback: Use the conditional, ending in -ais for je.
exercises.explanation: J’aimerais and je voudrais both express a wish in the conditional.

exercises.instruction: Turn this into a wish: put aimer in the conditional.
exercises.hint: Future stem of aimer plus the elle ending of the imparfait.
exercises.feedback: Change aime into the conditional.
exercises.explanation: Aimer- + -ait gives elle aimerait, she would like.

exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: This is a wish, and the ending does not match tu.
exercises.explanation: With tu, the conditional ends in -ais: tu aimerais.

exercises.source: À ta place, je ____ ce travail.
exercises.hint: À ta place describes something imagined. Check the ending for je.
exercises.feedback: An imagined situation uses the conditional.
exercises.explanation: À ta place calls for the conditional: je prendrais.

exercises.source: Dans un monde idéal, tout le monde ____ (avoir) une maison.
exercises.hint: Tout le monde takes the il form. Avoir has an irregular stem.
exercises.feedback: An imagined world calls for the conditional of avoir.
exercises.explanation: Aur- + -ait gives tout le monde aurait.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Start with À ta place.
exercises.source: If I were you (to a friend), I would leave (partir).

alternatives.message: Je partirai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: The situation is imagined, so the verb is in the conditional.
exercises.feedback: Use the conditional of partir with je.
exercises.explanation: À ta place, je partirais: partir- + -ais.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the conditional to show it is only imagined.
exercises.source: Avec un jardin, nous faisons des barbecues.
answers: Avec un jardin, nous ferions des barbecues.
exercises.hint: Faire has an irregular stem in the conditional.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of faire with the nous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.explanation: Fer- + -ions gives nous ferions: we would have barbecues.

exercises.instruction: Fix the verb: this situation is only imagined.
exercises.source: Sans téléphone, je serai plus calme.
answers: Sans téléphone, je serais plus calme.
exercises.hint: An imagined situation needs would, not will.
exercises.feedback: Serai is the future.
exercises.explanation: Would be is the conditional: je serais.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the conditional.
exercises.source: In his place, she would say no.
answers: À sa place, elle dirait non.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of dire. Only one is the conditional.
exercises.feedback: Dira is the future. Would is the conditional.
exercises.explanation: Dir- + -ait gives elle dirait.

exercises.source: Je te le promets : demain, je te ____ ma réponse.
exercises.hint: A promise about tomorrow says what will happen.
exercises.feedback: This is a certain future event, not an imagined one.
exercises.explanation: Will give is the future: je donnerai. Donnerais would mean would give.

exercises.hint: Quand j’étais petit describes a past habit.
exercises.feedback: A past habit uses the imparfait, which has no r of the future stem.
exercises.explanation: Used to read is the imparfait: je lisais.

exercises.instruction: Change the future into the conditional.
exercises.source: Avec ton aide, je finirai ce soir.
answers: Avec ton aide, je finirais ce soir.
exercises.hint: Keep the stem and change only the ending.
exercises.feedback: The conditional has the future stem plus the imparfait ending.
exercises.explanation: Je finirai (will) becomes je finirais (would): the ending -ai becomes -ais.

exercises.instruction: Write pleuvoir in the right tense: imparfait, future or conditional.
exercises.source: Hier, il ____ (pleuvoir) quand je suis sorti.
exercises.hint: Hier sets a background scene in the past, behind je suis sorti.
exercises.feedback: The scene is in the past, so neither the future stem nor the conditional fits.
exercises.explanation: A past background uses the imparfait: il pleuvait.

exercises.instruction: Fix the verb: this situation is only imagined.
exercises.source: À ta place, j’achèterai cette veste.
answers: À ta place, j’achèterais cette veste.
exercises.hint: À ta place needs would, not will.
exercises.feedback: J’achèterai is the future.
exercises.explanation: Would buy is the conditional: j’achèterais.

alternatives.message: Je viendrai is the future (will). Would is the conditional, which ends in -rais, -rait, -rions, -riez or -raient.

exercises.hint: Would is the conditional: irregular stem of venir plus the je ending.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending: would needs -rais.
exercises.explanation: Viendr- + -ais gives je viendrais.
